source: NCERT Class XI, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch. 3 (Interior of the Earth).

sections.heading: 1. Sources of Information
points: **Direct sources:** rocks from mining, deep drilling (e.g. Kola borehole), volcanic eruptions.
**Indirect sources:** temperature/pressure/density with depth, meteorites, gravitation, magnetic field, and above all **seismic (earthquake) waves**.
Seismic waves reveal the layered structure of the Earth.

sections.heading: 2. Earthquakes and Seismic Waves
points: An **earthquake** = shaking of the earth due to release of energy along a **fault**; origin = **focus/hypocentre**, point above on surface = **epicentre**.

sub: **P-waves (Primary)** — fastest, longitudinal, travel through **solids, liquids and gases**.
**S-waves (Secondary)** — transverse, travel **only through solids** (do not pass through the liquid outer core → 'shadow zone').
**L-waves (Surface)** — most destructive, travel along the surface.

points: The **S-wave shadow zone** proves the **outer core is liquid**.

sections.heading: 3. Layers of the Earth's Interior
points: **Crust** — thin outermost layer; **continental crust (SIAL)** and **oceanic crust (SIMA, denser)**; separated from mantle by the **Mohorovicic (Moho) discontinuity**.
**Mantle** — extends to ~2900 km; the **asthenosphere** (source of magma) lies in the upper mantle; the **Gutenberg discontinuity** separates mantle and core.
**Core** — **outer core (liquid)** and **inner core (solid)**; composed mainly of **iron and nickel (NIFE)**; source of Earth's magnetism.

sections.heading: 4. Volcanoes and Volcanic Landforms
points: A **volcano** = a vent through which molten material (lava), gases and ash erupt.
Types: **shield, composite, cinder cone, caldera**; **hot spots** (e.g. Hawaii).
**Intrusive forms** (below surface): **batholith, laccolith, sill, dyke**; **extrusive**: lava flows, plateaus (Deccan Traps).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: P-waves = fastest, through solid/liquid/gas; S-waves = only solids.
S-wave shadow zone proves the outer core is liquid.
Crust: SIAL (continental) + SIMA (oceanic); Moho separates crust and mantle.
Core = iron + nickel (NIFE); outer core liquid, inner core solid.
Intrusive forms: batholith, laccolith, sill, dyke; Deccan Traps = lava plateau.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **S-waves travel only through solids** — their shadow zone shows the **outer core is liquid**.
**Moho discontinuity** = crust–mantle boundary; **Gutenberg** = mantle–core.
**Focus = origin inside earth; epicentre = point on surface above it.**
The core is made mainly of **iron and nickel (NIFE)**.
